metadata.scenario_context: Emily is preparing to move into a new home and is planning to host a housewarming party. One of her neighbors have heavy drinkers . Mike and Kim will attend Emily’s housewarming party.

cultural_axis.agent_1_value: People from China would like to have heavy drinkers as neighbors.
cultural_axis.agent_2_value: People from Taiwan ROC would not like to have heavy drinkers as neighbors.

agent_1.goal_1: Discuss bringing chrysanthemums to Emily’s housewarming party
agent_1.goal_2: Question whether would like to have heavy drinkers as a neighbor.

agent_2.goal_1: Decide appropriate gift to bring to Emily’s housewarming party.
agent_2.goal_2: Discuss on whether it’s acceptable to have heavy drinkers  as a neighbor.

shared_prefix.speaker: Mike
shared_prefix.message:
Hey Kim, do you think we should bring something nice for Emily's housewarming? I was thinking maybe some chrysanthemums. They’re pretty and symbolize good luck, right? 

Also, what do you think about her neighbors? I heard they’re heavy drinkers... but honestly, I think having neighbors like that can be fun. What’s your take?
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Kim
shared_prefix.message:
Chrysanthemums sound nice... but maybe something more practical, like a nice kitchen item? I think she’d appreciate that. 

As for the neighbors, heavy drinkers? That's... not ideal. I mean, in Taiwan, we value a peaceful living environment. It's tough to feel comfortable with that kind of noise and chaos next door.
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Mike
shared_prefix.message:
I get that a kitchen item is practical, but I still think chrysanthemums would brighten up her new place. They really bring a good vibe. 

As for the heavy drinkers, I see where you're coming from. But honestly, having lively neighbors can make things more interesting. A little noise isn’t always a bad thing, right? It can bring a sense of community.
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Kim
shared_prefix.message:
I understand your point about the chrysanthemums... but we should consider what she needs. Practical gifts often mean more in a new home.

Regarding the heavy drinkers, I just can't see it that way. A lively atmosphere can quickly turn into a disruptive one. Community is important, but not at the expense of a peaceful home life.
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Mike
shared_prefix.message:
I see your point about practical gifts, and I really think chrysanthemums can be a nice touch, too. But I get it—helping her settle in is key.

As for the neighbors, I think it’s interesting how we view them differently. Deep down, we are all the same, wanting a good community. I guess some values are just universal. A little liveliness can actually bring people together, don’t you think? When you really get to know people, they're pretty much like us, and that can create a friendly environment.
shared_prefix.label: Minimization
